claims.implementation: backend/arkali/engineering/localai/adapter.py declares LocalRuntimeAdapter, a structural Protocol (runtime_checkable), and the value objects it trades in (LocalModelDescriptor, RuntimeProbeResult, InferenceResult). ollama_adapter.py and openai_compatible_adapter.py are two real, structurally distinct adapters: different transport (Ollama's native /api/* surface vs. the OpenAI-compatible /v1/* surface), different default endpoint, different request/response envelope, sharing no transport code and each loopback-only by construction (LocalRuntimeTargetNotLoopbackError refuses a non-loopback endpoint at __init__). Neither adapter module imports the other's transport internals, and no sibling module in engineering.localai imports a concrete adapter class directly - every caller depends on the Protocol.

claims.implementation: host_probe.py provides real, read-only host/runtime/hardware probes (CPU count, total RAM via GlobalMemoryStatusEx on Windows, GPU presence via a read-only nvidia-smi query, and real adapter reachability) mirroring control.isolation.backend_probe's own read-only-probe guarantee. suitability.py judges a real installed model's fit from a conservative, quantization-derived RAM estimate against 60% of the host's total probed RAM - CPU-only is always a valid answer, and the verdict is proven identical whether or not an accelerator is reported present (never assumed, never required). capability_exposure.py builds a real C-13 CapabilityNode whose configured_state is CONFIGURED only when both the real runtime probe and the real suitability verdict independently resolved PASS - earned, never defaulted, and carrying no provider-owned field. network_policy.py proves the Local-Only negative control against the real, unmodified PDP (a hypothetical non-loopback local-AI target is honestly ASK_USER outside Local-Only and DENY inside), while this phase's own adapters never construct such a target and never import control.policy for their own loopback traffic - independence from Local-Only state, not a policy exemption, is what 'Local AI remains available' means here.

deferred.reason: NOT_APPLICABLE per its own Appendix A rule: `ARK-REQ-0129 applicable AND dataset.verified_count > 0`. The first conjunct is true (see ARK-REQ-0129's claim above); the second is honestly false - a repository-wide scan (test_phase_22_journey.py::TestCondition0130DatasetVerificationDoesNotExist) confirms no module anywhere under backend/arkali/ contains the word 'dataset', so no dataset-verification authority exists to report a nonzero verified count, and engineering.localai declares no fine-tuning or distillation capability of its own (a second scan confirms no 'fine_tun'/'finetun'/'distill' marker exists in this context's source). Building a dataset-verification authority to force this predicate true would be scope creep this phase does not own - REQUIREMENT_REGISTER.md's own CONDITIONAL vocabulary treats an honestly-false applicability rule as NOT_APPLICABLE, not as an obligation to construct the missing authority.
